item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 211144
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Wed Oct 21 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

South of Southern Mexico (EP94):
Satellite imagery indicates that a low-pressure system located a few
hundred miles south-southwest of the Gulf of Tehuantepec is
producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms. This activity
continues to become better organized, and if current trends
persist, a tropical depression is expected to form later today. The
system is expected to move westward to west-northwestward at around
10 mph during the next few days, well offshore the coast of
southern Mexico. For additional information, including Gale
Warnings, see the High Seas Forecast issued by the National Weather
Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form in the far western
central Pacific a few hundred miles southwest of Johnson Atoll late
this weekend of early next week. Environmental conditions appear
conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the system
moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Wed Oct 21 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 211436
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Twenty-Two-E Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 AM CST Wed Oct 21 2026
 
...TROPICAL DEPRESSION FORMS SOUTH OF SOUTHERN MEXICO...
...FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...9.5N 99.3W
ABOUT 515 MI...825 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 735 MI...1185 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 265 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Twenty-Two-E was located near latitude 9.5 North, longitude 99.3
West. The depression is moving toward the west near 7 mph (11 km/h)
and this general slow forward motion with a turn towards the 
northwest then north-northwest is expected the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Steady to rapid intensification is expected, and the system is 
forecast to become a hurricane on Friday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Tropical Depression Twenty-Two-E are 
expected to begin affecting portions of the coast of southern and 
southwestern Mexico this weekend and continue into next week.  These 
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Depression Twenty-Two-E Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Wed Oct 21 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 211437
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Depression Twenty-Two-E Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 AM CST Wed Oct 21 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the disturbance located south of 
southern Mexico (EP94) has continued to become better organized this 
morning. Deep convection has increased, and showers and 
thunderstorms have become more concentrated within curved banding 
features. A subjective Dvorak satellite intensity estimate from TAFB 
was T2.0/ 30 kt. Visible satellite shows that the low-level 
circulation center is now well-defined, and advisories are therefore 
being initiated on Tropical Depression Twenty-Two-E. The initial 
intensity is set at 30 kt for this advisory.
 
The initial motion is estimated at 265/6 kt. A generally slow 
forward motion is expected with a turn towards the northwest and 
then north-northwest as the cyclone is steered along the southern 
and western periphery of a mid-level ridge located over Mexico. The 
NHC track forecast leans towards the GDMI and HCCA solutions and is 
on the eastern side of the guidance envelope. The GFS and some of 
the hurricane regional models continue to move the system more 
southwestward over the next 12 hours or so and are on the western 
portion of the track suite. 

Environmental conditions are highly conducive for rapid 
intensification. The cyclone is located over very warm waters in the 
eastern Pacific within an environment of low vertical wind shear, 
abundant mid-level moisture, and divergence aloft. Rapid 
intensification guidance is also well above climatological mean, 
particularly in the 12-60 h period. In fact, the GFS and ECMWF SHIPS 
RI probabilities for a 55-kt increase in 48 hours are 73 and 83 
percent, respectively. Thus, rapid intensification is explicitly 
forecast during that time. By 72 hours, vertical wind shear is 
forecast to increase, and mid-level dry air could begin to entrain 
into the circulation. As a result, a weakening trend is shown later 
in the forecast period. The official NHC intensity forecast is near 
the upper end of the guidance, although the Google DeepMind does 
show a higher peak intensity.
